print.notes: Picture on PDF p.383; verses 2 and 3 are printed with an explicit leading verse number ('2.' / '3.'), which is what rule 13.11.4.a's cell-5 heading treatment is transcribing; verse 1 carries no printed number since it is given with the music instead.
print.printFeatures: Bold title; musical staff notation for verse 1; verses 2-3 printed as plain numbered prose-style stanzas below the music.

braille.notes: Verbatim from .txt lines 11042-11055, after stripping a 5-char line-number field (2-digit max line number 14, +3=5) and converting U+2800. Title (line 1) is centred; verse 1 (lines 3-6) is transcribed with no verse-number heading (matching print, which gives it none). Verse numbers '2' and '3' (lines 8 and 12) are given as cell-5 headings ('#b4' = '2.', '#c4' = '3.', 4-cell/cell-5 indent), per rule 13.11.4.a; each verse's first line only is shown, followed by a '444' continuation marker showing the excerpt deliberately omits the remaining three lines of each verse (which the source's print does include in full).

uncertain: Only the first line of verses 2 and 3 is transcribed in this excerpt (each followed by '444'), even though print shows all four lines of each verse; recorded as a deliberate excerpt (matching the source's own truncation), not a transcription gap.
resolution: Index 0 ('On Top of Old Smokey', ref '1', .txt line 11042) needed a NEW value neither run had: 8 leading blank cells (run A had 0, run B had 10) -- counted directly against the source (reference field 5 characters, 2-digit max '14' + 3; then 8 literal U+2800 characters before the text). The remaining 13 lines were already identical between runs and independently confirmed correct. CORRECTION during buildModel13 integration: run A recorded the verse numbers '2'/'3' as the `number` field on the FIRST line of stanzas 2/3 (implying they are folded into that line's own text, per BANA 13.11.4a/F-P3); run B recorded no number at all. The gold braille (.txt lines 11051/11055 region) settles this: '2.'/'3.' are each their OWN separate braille line ('    #b4' / '    #c4', 4 leading cells = level 2), printed BEFORE the stanza's first verse line (which itself carries no prefix at all, 0 leading cells) -- not folded into it. Modelled here as two synthetic poem lines ('2.' / '3.', indent 2) inserted ahead of stanzas 2/3, replacing the `number` field on their first real line. print text for these two lines otherwise kept as run A gave it (no comma after 'rob you', matching the braille's own lack of trailing punctuation there).
